subject: Re: Redwood Pricing + Batching assumptions — follow-up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechflow.com>, Priya Singh <priya@fintechflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood — pricing & batching follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on how FintechFlow uses LLMs for transaction categorization and the in-app assistant. I wanted to capture the key items and next steps so we can size costs and propose a target pricing range.

Recap of what you shared (please correct me if I missed anything):
- Primary workload: automated categorization + short assistant replies.
- Traffic pattern: steady daytime traffic (US business hours) with periodic bursts triggered by batch reprocessing jobs.
- Latency expectations: p50 ~ 150-250ms for short completions; p95 can be higher for long-context jobs.
- Typical sequence length: ~350-500 tokens for assistant flows; categorization requests average ~120 tokens.
- Concurrency: ~40 sustained reqs/sec during peak hour; occasional spikes to ~180 reqs/sec for reconciliation batch windows.
- Monthly token estimate (rough): you mentioned ~1.5B tokens / month but said there is +/- 20% uncertainty.

A few specific asks so we can model unit economics:
1) Can you confirm the 1.5B monthly token estimate, and whether that includes both input+output tokens?
2) What budget range would signal a buy (monthly committed spend)? Rough band is helpful (e.g., <$10k / month, $10-30k, $30-75k, etc.).
3) Any hard SLOs (latency/p95) for the assistant beyond what we discussed?

Preliminary notes on batching and unit economics (for discussion):
- Continuous batching: with a steady stream we typically see 20-45% token cost reductions compared to no-batching, depending on sequence lengths and inter-request gaps. For your mix (short categorization + medium assistant), assume ~30-35% improvement as a working number.
- Concurrency impact: sustained concurrency (40 rps) is easy to handle with dedicated capacity; spikes to ~180 rps will need either autoscaling/burst capacity or routing to lower-cost variants.
- Target $/1M tokens: I want to understand what target unit price makes sense for FintechFlow. For rough context, our public hosted tiers start higher, but committed/reserved volume can get to competitive $/1M token targets — we can propose specific bands after you confirm volume and budget.

Next steps: if you can reply with (1) confirmed monthly tokens (input+output), (2) target monthly budget range, and (3) whether you want a committed/reserved pricing quote vs consumption-based, I’ll put together a short pricing model + suggested config (model variant, batching window, concurrency settings) and loop in Aditya for a technical sizing.

I’ve attached a quick MAU/usage template (mau_estimates.csv) you can fill, and I’ll attach a draft pricing grid in my follow-up.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai

Camila — thanks for the summary and template. Quick answers inline.

On Tue, Aug 18, 2026 at 9:15 AM Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai> wrote:
> - Monthly token estimate (rough): you mentioned ~1.5B tokens / month but said there is +/- 20% uncertainty.

Yes — 1.5B is a fair baseline and that is input+output. Could be as low as 1.2B or as high as 1.8B depending on feature rollout.

> 1) Can you confirm the 1.5B monthly token estimate, and whether that includes both input+output tokens?

Confirmed: input+output included.

> 2) What budget range would signal a buy (monthly committed spend)?

We’re looking to qualify feasibility internally. Rough budget band for the initial contract would be $15k-–35k/month. If unit economics look great and we can hit p50 latency targets, we can expand faster.

> 3) Any hard SLOs (latency/p95) for the assistant beyond what we discussed?

p50 target is ~150-200ms for assistant replies; p95 target is less strict (can be up to ~800ms), but categorization must be reliable and <300ms p95.

I attached a filled version of the MAU/usage template — the file is mau_estimates.csv. We can also share a short anonymized sample trace if that helps.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform, FintechFlow
alex.chen@fintechflow.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechflow.com>, Priya Singh <priya@fintechflow.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood — pricing & batching follow-up

Thanks Alex — this is super helpful. I reviewed your MAU file — using 1.5B tokens/month (input+output) and your traffic/concurrency profile, here are two starter approaches we often use for customers in your band:

Option A — Committed (reserved) capacity — recommended if you want predictable unit economics and lower $/1M tokens:
- Assumption: 1.2-1.8B tokens/month with a 12-month commit.
- Expected unit price band (example): $650-–1,200 per 1M tokens depending on model variant + quantization profile.
- Continuous batching expectation: ~30-35% effective token-cost reduction for your workload; included in the recommendation.
- Latency: p50 targets easily met with reserved pools; p95 for long-context jobs will vary but we can tune batching/windowing to prioritize p95 when needed.

Option B — Consumption (pay-as-you-go) with burstable dedicated pools — recommended if you prefer flexibility:
- Higher $/1M tokens (approx 15-35% premium over reserved).
- We'll set autoscaling thresholds for peaks (180 rps) and fall back to compatible lower-cost variants for large batch windows.

Unit economics and target: based on your $15k-–35k/month guidance, to make a meaningful reserved discount we’d be aiming for a unit target in the $700-–1,000 per 1M tokens range at the lower end of the commit band. If you’re targeting sub-$700/1M tokens, we’d need larger commit or longer term (or model/quantization changes).

Technical notes (high-level):
- Continuous batching: expect best results when requests have small inter-arrival times — this aligns with your daytime steady traffic. For mixed workloads (short + medium sequences) the ~30% estimate is conservative.
- Concurrency ops: sustain 40 rps easily on a small dedicated pool; for spikes to 180 rps we recommend burst capacity or routing to a slightly lower-quality variant; can also use short-lived ephemeral capacity for reconciliation jobs.

Attached: redwood_pricing_grid.pdf (example pricing bands + options). I’m looping in Aditya for the technical sizing (batch window, per-GPU throughput, KV caching).

If this looks reasonable, I can put together a one-page mutual action plan and an initial committed quote by early next week.

Best,
Camila

Alex — quick technical note to supplement Camila’s email: 

- Continuous batching behavior: best when the steady-state inter-arrival time is <20-40ms; with that you can maintain small batch windows (lower latency) while still getting most batching benefits. If your daytime stream has gaps >100ms, batching efficiency drops and we see lower token-cost savings.
- Recommended batch window for your mix: 25-50ms to balance p50 latency and batching.
- Concurrency sizing: on our recommended GPU profile, expect ~200-400 tokens/sec per GPU for mixed short/medium sequences; peg concurrency per GPU to keep GPU utilization ~60-80% for steady traffic.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for assistant flows to reduce repeated prompt cost on multi-turn interactions. This typically improves effective throughput for assistant sessions by 15-25%.

Happy to run a short sizing exercise on the sample trace you mentioned — if you can share an anonymized trace or a short request-timestamp sample, we’ll produce a 1-page technical sizing.





— Aditya
